newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada agrees to help troubled Canadian Air.
newsitem.headline: Canada agrees to help troubled Canadian Air.

text.p: Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson said on Wednesday Canada and two provincial governments had agreed to a one-month delay in repayments of capital from troubled Canadian Airlines.
He also said the federal government would seriously examine any proposal by AMR Corp to increase its minority shareholding in Canadian, though it would not necessarily agree to allow it.
"The federal government along with many other creditors has been asked for a delay in repayment in capital," Anderson told reporters.

Canadian has C$30 million left of the original C$120 million provided by Canada and the provincial governments, he added, though he was not immediately sure what proportion of the remainder was due this month.
"They simply asked us to slide that for a month. They'll continue to pay interest. We're quite willing to accede to that, as have the other two governments involved," he said.
Other creditors have acted similarly, Anderson added.
Canadian said on Friday it was in financial trouble, and would seek concessions from its unions and from AMR Corp , parent of American Airlines.

AMR said it had no plans to increase its investment in Canadian, but if it wanted to it would require federal exemption from a rule limiting non-Canadian ownership of Canadian airlines' voting shares to 25 percent.

Anderson, asked if Ottawa would agree to raise the limit for AMR, said the question was hypothetical since no request had been made. But he added: "Of course a serious proposal from any airline would be looked at seriously. It doesn't mean to say we'd accept it."
